original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it.

first_step.inspect: Read Model section 1 of the three-register bound and identify the exact excluded free operations.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Write a complete operation alphabet outside one named premise and price a baseline before searching identities.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.

actual_scope: In the formal group algebra K[(Z/2)^3], for every set of four distinct nonzero addresses on four data registers, compare the unit paid-gate count with the rank-one gate count and the total projector rank, allowing finite workspace and fixed free scalar maps.
scope_change_reason: The assigned card allows a larger register count outside the rational three-register model. Four data registers and the finite address group (Z/2)^3 replace M_3(Q) rank-one frames. This is the smallest width at which four distinct nonzero addresses can separate a unit-gate bill from a rank-one bill; the rational three-register theorem does not apply, and the three-label group-algebra cut does not decide four labels.
bottleneck_link: Side result on the bit register interface, not a supplier admission. A three-gate word looks cheaper if every projector costs one, but every such word has total rank at least 5, while four rank-one coordinate gates cost total rank 4. Adopting the shorter word would not improve a rank-charged bit primitive. No selected moment or kappa changes.
stop_rule: Stop after the (Z/2)^3 four-address floor and its direct matching constructions. Do not search A4, extra generators, or a native supplier in this session.
evidence: Self-contained support and character argument. The new comparison is that every three-gate word has total rank at least 5, so ranks (2,1,1) are impossible, while four rank-one gates have total rank 4. Checked on all 35 quadruples, 168 bases and 512 label triples in three algebras. Marker PASS_ELEMENTARY_ABELIAN_FOUR_LABEL_FLOOR.
author: AI-assisted research session
ai_assistance: Substantial AI assistance was used to derive the argument, write the verifier, and check the finite cases. Assistance is disclosed without naming a coding-agent product. One Discussion comment attempt was forbidden and was not retried.

open_questions.question: For four distinct non-identity elements of A4, is the rank-one gate count still four when every homomorphism to Z/2 is trivial?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The separation proved here uses a surjection onto (Z/2)^3. A4 is the smallest nonabelian group whose 2-abelianization is trivial, so a length-three rank-one word there would be real compression that this quotient cannot see.
open_questions.first_step: Fix four 3-cycles that lie in one ordered three-label subproduct set and test the coordinate normal form D(E_11, g) C1 D(E_11, h) C2 D(E_11, k) over F2 with a finite generating set of scalar maps, or find a C3-valued coefficient cut whose rank is at least 2.
open_questions.blocked_by: Free scalar maps are infinite. A finite normal form or a new quotient identity is required before an exhaustive search is a proof.
